verses.text: After this, David defeated the Philistines and brought them under his control. He took Metheg Ammah, their main city, out of the Philistines' hands.

He also defeated Moab. He made the prisoners lie down on the ground and measured them off with a cord. Two lengths of the cord were put to death, and one full length were allowed to live. So the Moabites became David's servants and paid him taxes.
David also defeated Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, when Hadadezer went to take back control along the Euphrates River.
David captured one thousand seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers from him. He crippled all the chariot horses, but kept enough of them for one hundred chariots.
When the Syrians from Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David killed twenty-two thousand of them.
Then David put groups of soldiers in the Syrian kingdom of Damascus, and the Syrians became his servants and paid him taxes. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
David took the gold shields that Hadadezer's officers carried and brought them to Jerusalem.
From Betah and Berothai, towns that belonged to Hadadezer, King David took a large amount of bronze.
Toi king of Hamath heard that David had defeated Hadadezer's whole army.

So Toi sent his son Joram to King David to greet him and congratulate him for fighting and defeating Hadadezer, because Hadadezer had been at war with Toi. Joram brought gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
King David gave these gifts to the LORD, together with the silver and gold he had taken from all the nations he had conquered:
from Syria, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek. He also gave the goods he had taken from Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
David became famous after he came back from killing eighteen thousand Syrians in the Valley of Salt.
He put groups of soldiers all through Edom, and all the Edomites became David's servants. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
David ruled over all Israel, and he did what was fair and right for all his people.
Joab son of Zeruiah was in charge of the army. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the official records.
Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests. Seraiah was the royal secretary.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the Kerethites and Pelethites, the king's guards. And David's sons were his chief officials.
